saints.name: St. John Neumann
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A Bohemian immigrant and Redemptorist who became bishop of Philadelphia and built up the American parochial schools…
biography: Born in 1811 at Prachatice in Bohemia, John Neumann studied at Budweis and Prague, then landed in New York in 1836 with one tattered suit and a dollar, seeking ordination. Bishop Dubois, in need of German priests, ordained him seventeen days later, and for four years he tramped the German missions around Buffalo, building churches and schools.

In 1840 he joined the Redemptorists, the first member of that congregation professed in America, and in 1852 he was consecrated fourth bishop of Philadelphia. There he organized the first diocesan school system in the United States, built churches at the rate of nearly one a month, and introduced the Forty Hours devotion to his adopted country.

Himself an immigrant at home in eight languages, he founded parishes for the newcomers, including the first Italian national parishes in the country, and he remains a patron of immigrants and of Catholic education. He collapsed and died on a Philadelphia street on 5 January 1860, aged forty-eight. Canonized by Pope Paul VI on 19 June 1977, he is the first American bishop raised to the altars.
saints.knownFor: Organizing the Catholic parochial-school system in America.
